ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the line $y=-\frac{1}{2}x-1$ intersects with the line $y=-2x+2$ at point $P$, and intersects with the $x$-axis at points $A$ and $B$, respectively. What are the coordinates of the intersection point $P$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given, we have $\begin{cases}y=-\frac{1}{2}x-1 \\ y=-2x+2\end{cases}$,\\
Solving this, we get $\begin{cases}x=2 \\ y=-2\end{cases}$,\\
$\therefore \boxed{P\left(2, -2\right)}$.

Use the text equations to find the x-intercepts: for y = -1/2 x - 1, set y=0 to get A = (-2, 0); for y = -2x + 2, set y=0 to get B = (1, 0).
